proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(f(x)=E_P[D\mid X=x]\).  By ass:observable-holder-extensions at \(s=1\), the two one-sided extensions are \(M\)-Lipschitz.  Let \(a=f(c_P-)\), \(d=f(c_P+)-f(c_P-)=d_P\), and define
\[
 e(x)=\begin{cases}
 f(x)-a,&x<c_P,\\
 f(x)-a-d,&x\ge c_P.
 \end{cases}
\]
The two pieces vanish at \(c_P\).  Hence each is \(M\)-Lipschitz on its side, and, if \(x<c_P<y\),
\[
 |e(y)-e(x)|\le M(y-c_P)+M(c_P-x)=M(y-x).
\]
Thus \(e\) is globally \(M\)-Lipschitz and
\[
 f(x)=a+d\mathbf 1\{x\ge c_P\}+e(x). \tag{1}
\]
Uniformity of \(X\), from ass:uniform-running-variable, and \(\int_0^1K_0(u)\,du=1\) give
\[
 \Delta_H^D(t)=d\left(1-\frac{|t-c_P|}{H}\right)_++Q_e(t),
 \qquad
 Q_e(t)=\frac1H\int_0^H\{e(t+x)-e(t-x)\}\,dx. \tag{2}
\]
The Lipschitz property yields
\[
 |Q_e(t)|\le MH,
 \qquad |Q_e(t)-Q_e(q)|\le2M|t-q|. \tag{3}
\]
There is a point \(q\in\mathcal G_H\) with \(|q-c_P|\le H/64\), including at the trimmed endpoints.  Since \(d\ge\kappa_n\) by ass:local-compliance-strength and \(MH=\kappa_n/2^{12}\), equations (2)--(3) imply
\[
 \Delta_H^D(q)\ge\frac{63}{64}\kappa_n-\frac{\kappa_n}{2^{12}},
 \qquad
 \sup_{|t-c_P|\ge H}|\Delta_H^D(t)|\le\frac{\kappa_n}{2^{12}}. \tag{4}
\]

For fixed \(t\), one summand in \(\widehat\Delta_{1,H}^D(t)\) has absolute value at most \(H^{-1}\) and second moment at most \(2H^{-1}\).  Its centered version is bounded by \(2H^{-1}\).  Independence from ass:iid-sampling and the elementary inequality
\[
 e^z\le1+z+\frac{z^2}{2(1-|z|/3)},\qquad |z|<3,
\]
give, by multiplying the conditional moment-generating-function bounds and optimizing the exponential parameter,
\[
 P\left\{\left|m^{-1}\sum_{i\in F_1}(W_i-E_PW_i)\right|>x\right\}
 \le2\exp\left\{-\frac{mx^2}{4/H+4x/(3H)}\right\}. \tag{5}
\]
At \(x=\kappa_n/16\le1\), the right side is at most \(2\exp\{-2^{-11}mH\kappa_n^2\}\).  The union bound over \(N_H\) grid points, with \(N_H=1+\lfloor32/H\rfloor\le1+32/H\), proves the first display of the lemma.  On \(\mathcal E_1\), equation (4) and two deviations of size \(\kappa_n/16\) show that no point at distance at least \(H\) can be within \(\kappa_n/8\) of the empirical maximum.  Thus every retained center is within \(H\) of \(c_P\), and its \(H\)-neighborhood is contained in \([c_P-2H,c_P+2H]\).

For \(|t-c_P|\le H\), equations (2)--(3) and \(H=\kappa_n/(2^{12}M)\) give
\[
 \Delta_H^D(c_P)-\Delta_H^D(t)
 \ge\left(\frac{\kappa_n}{H}-2M\right)|t-c_P|
 \ge\frac{\kappa_n}{2H}|t-c_P|. \tag{6}
\]
For \(H\le|t-c_P|\le2H\), the same equations give a loss at least \(\kappa_n/2\).  Let \(c_n\in\mathcal G_n(B_H)\) satisfy \(|c_n-c_P|\le1/n\).  Such a point exists on \(\mathcal E_1\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), because the retained coarse cell containing the \(H/64\)-approximation to \(c_P\) contains an open neighborhood of \(c_P\).  The Lipschitz constant of the right side of (2) is at most \(2\kappa_n/H+2M\), so, whenever \(u\ge16/n\), the grid error is at most one quarter of the lower bound in (6).

It remains to control the local maximizer.  For \(t>c_n\), the difference of the two rectangular kernel weights is supported on the three moving boundary strips at \(c_n-H,c_n,c_n+H\); the middle strip has coefficient two and the other two have coefficient one.  Up to displacement \(r\), its integrated squared weight is at most \(6r/H^2\) and its absolute weight is at most \(2/H\).  Reveal the observations in each strip in increasing \(X\)-order.  The same exponential inequality used for (5), stopped at the first crossing of the line \(\kappa_n r/(8H)\), gives, on \(2^ju\le r<2^{j+1}u\),
\[
 P\left\{
 \sup_{2^ju\le t-c_n<2^{j+1}u}
 \left[(\overline\Delta_H^D-E_P\overline\Delta_H^D)(t)
 -(\overline\Delta_H^D-E_P\overline\Delta_H^D)(c_n)\right]
 \ge\frac{\kappa_n2^ju}{8H}
 \right\}
 \le2e^{-2^{-13}m\kappa_n^2 2^ju}, \tag{7}
\]
where \(\overline\Delta_H^D=(\widehat\Delta_{2,H}^D+\widehat\Delta_{3,H}^D)/2\).  Indeed, before the crossing the product moment-generating function is at most
\[
 \exp\{12m\eta^2(2^{j+1}u)/H^2\};
\]
choosing \(\eta=\kappa_nH/2^7\), using \(\kappa_n\le1/8\), and applying Markov's inequality gives (7).  Decreasing \(X\)-order gives the identical left-tail inequality.  Equations (6)--(7), the absorbed grid error, and summation of the two geometric series in \(j\) yield
\[
 P\bigl(\{|\widehat c-c_P|>u\}\cap\mathcal E_1\bigr)
 \le9e^{-2^{-16}m\kappa_n^2u}.
\]
For \(u>2H\) the event on the left is empty by the already proved containment.  This proves the lemma for every \(u\ge16/n\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose \(s=1\).  Define \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}\) by def:lipschitz-scan-invert.  There are finite constants \(C_1,C_2\), displayed in the proof and depending only on \(M,v,\alpha\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), if \(T_n=n\kappa_n^3\ge C_1\log(e/\kappa_n)\), then \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}\) is uniformly honest over \(\mathcal P_n\) and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P|I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}|
 \le C_2\min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}\right\}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 L_n(\kappa_n)\asymp L_n^{\mathrm{known}}(\kappa_n)
 \asymp\min\left\{1,\frac{n^{-1/3}}{\kappa_n}\right\}
\]
throughout this Lipschitz strong-signal region, uniformly over vanishing \(\kappa_n\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 L_\alpha=\log(32/\alpha),\qquad A_\alpha=2^{16}L_\alpha,
\]
\[
 B_{M,\alpha}=1+\log\!\left(\frac{16(1+2^{17}M)}{\alpha}\right),
\]
and define
\[
 C_r=8M+16A_\alpha+1+16M(A_\alpha+1)+8\sqrt{L_\alpha},
\]
\[
 c_3=2^{-24}M^{-1},\qquad c_2=2^{-22},
\]
\[
 C_F=2(3ec_3)^{-1/3}+12(2ec_2)^{-1/2},
 \qquad C_2=16C_r+4C_F,
\]
and
\[
 C_1=\max\left\{
 2^{27}MB_{M,\alpha},\;
 2^{15}M(8A_\alpha+1),\;
 8(8C_r)^3,\;
 2^{30}ML_\alpha
 \right\}. \tag{8}
\]
These constants are finite because \(M<\infty\) and \(0<\alpha<1/4\).  They are deliberately conservative.

For sufficiently large \(n\), \(m\ge n/8\).  Since \(H=\kappa_n/(2^{12}M)\),
\[
 N_H\le1+\frac{2^{17}M}{\kappa_n},\qquad
 \log(16N_H/\alpha)\le B_{M,\alpha}\log(e/\kappa_n), \tag{9}
\]
and
\[
 2^{-11}mH\kappa_n^2\ge\frac{T_n}{2^{26}M}. \tag{10}
\]
The first entry of (8), the signal condition, and lem:rectangular-jump-scan-localization imply
\[
 P(\mathcal E_1^c)\le\alpha/8. \tag{11}
\]
The localization part of that lemma, with \(R_c=A_\alpha/(m\kappa_n^2)+1/n\), gives
\[
 P\bigl(\{|\widehat c-c_P|>R_c\}\cap\mathcal E_1\bigr)
 \le9e^{-L_\alpha}=\frac{9\alpha}{32}. \tag{12}
\]
Here \(R_c\ge16/n\), because \(m\le n/4\), \(\kappa_n\le1/8\), and \(A_\alpha>1\).

We next verify the deterministic fallbacks.  Let \(q=\kappa_n/b\).  Since \(b^{-3}=m\) and \(m\ge n/8\),
\[
 q^3=m\kappa_n^3\ge T_n/8. \tag{13}
\]
For \(q\ge1\), substitution into the definition of \(r_n\), together with \(1/n\le1/(4m)=b^3/4\), gives
\[
 r_n\le C_rb. \tag{14}
\]
Indeed, after division by \(b\), the four terms in \(r_n\) are bounded respectively by \(8M\), \(16A_\alpha+1\), \(16M(A_\alpha+1)\), and \(8\sqrt{L_\alpha}\).  Equations (8), (13), and (14) give \(r_n\le\kappa_n/8\).  Also
\[
 \frac{R_c}{H}=2^{12}M\left\{
 \frac{A_\alpha}{m\kappa_n^3}+\frac1{n\kappa_n}\right\}
 \le\frac{2^{12}M(8A_\alpha+1)}{T_n}\le\frac18. \tag{15}
\]
Thus both deterministic checks in def:lipschitz-scan-invert pass.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) and abbreviate \(\theta=\theta_P\).  By prop:wald-late-identification and binary potential outcomes, \(|\theta|\le1\), while the definition of \(\theta_P\) gives \(y_P-\theta d_P=0\); division is legitimate because ass:local-compliance-strength gives \(d_P\ge\kappa_n>0\).  The conditional regression of \(U=Y-\theta D\), separately on the two sides of \(c_P\), is therefore \(2M\)-Lipschitz and has zero level jump.  Gluing its one-sided extensions at their common value makes it globally \(2M\)-Lipschitz.  Conditional on folds one through three, \(\widehat c\) is fixed and fold four is independent by ass:iid-sampling.  Hence, on \(|\widehat c-c_P|\le R_c\),
\[
 \left|E_P[\widehat y(\widehat c)-\theta\widehat d(\widehat c)
 \mid F_1,F_2,F_3]\right|\le2Mb. \tag{16}
\]
For treatment, equations (1)--(3) in lem:rectangular-jump-scan-localization, now at bandwidth \(b\), give
\[
 \left|E_P[\widehat d(\widehat c)\mid F_1,F_2,F_3]-d_P\right|
 \le Mb+\frac{2\kappa_nR_c}{b}+2MR_c. \tag{17}
\]
All divisions are valid because \(b>0\).  Moreover, \(16\kappa_nR_c/b\le r_n\le\kappa_n/8\) gives \(R_c/b\le1/128\), so the displaced cutoff lies inside the kernel window.

The fold-four summands are bounded and are nonzero only when \(|X-\widehat c|\le b\), an event of probability at most \(2b\) by ass:uniform-running-variable.  Since \(|U|\le2\), their conditional second moments are at most \(8\lVert K_0\rVert_\infty^2/b\) for \(U\) and \(2\lVert K_0\rVert_\infty^2/b\) for \(D\).  Applying the moment-generating-function calculation (5), conditionally on the first three folds, yields simultaneously
\[
 \left|\widehat\Delta_{4,b}^{U}(\widehat c)
 -E_P[\widehat\Delta_{4,b}^{U}(\widehat c)\mid F_1,F_2,F_3]\right|
 \le8\lVert K_0\rVert_\infty\sqrt{\frac{L_\alpha}{mb}}, \tag{18}
\]
and the analogous treatment inequality with constant four, except on an event of probability at most \(\alpha/8\).  The Bernstein linear terms are absorbed by the displayed square-root terms for all sufficiently large \(n\), since \(mb=m^{2/3}\to\infty\).  Equations (16)--(18) and the definition of \(r_n\) imply
\[
 |\widehat y(\widehat c)-\theta_P\widehat d(\widehat c)|\le2r_n. \tag{19}
\]
If \(\widehat d(\widehat c)<\kappa_n/2\), the rule returns \(\Theta\), which contains \(\theta_P\); otherwise (19) puts \(\theta_P\) in the accepted set.  Equations (11), (12), and (18) bound the total failure probability by
\[
 \frac\alpha8+\frac{9\alpha}{32}+\frac\alpha8
 =\frac{17\alpha}{32}<\alpha.
\]
The bound is independent of \(P\), proving uniform honesty.

For expected length, whenever \(\widehat d(\widehat c)\ge\kappa_n/2\), the accepted labels form an interval of length at most
\[
 \frac{4r_n}{\widehat d(\widehat c)}\le\frac{8r_n}{\kappa_n}. \tag{20}
\]
On \(|\widehat c-c_P|\le b/8\), equation (17) with \(R_c\) replaced by \(b/8\), the bound \(Mb\le r_n/8\le\kappa_n/64\), and a fold-four treatment fluctuation at most \(\kappa_n/8\) imply \(\widehat d(\widehat c)>\kappa_n/2\).  Let \(\mathcal F_n\) be the event that the rule invokes its full-length scan or denominator fallback.  This event is contained in a coarse-scan failure, a localization error larger than \(b/8\), or a fold-four treatment deviation larger than \(\kappa_n/8\).  Equations (5), (9)--(13), and lem:rectangular-jump-scan-localization give
\[
 P(\mathcal F_n)
 \le2e^{-c_3q^3}+12e^{-c_2q^2}. \tag{21}
\]
The numerical slack in \(c_3=2^{-24}M^{-1}\) absorbs \(N_H\) under the first signal inequality in (8); the localization exponent at \(b/8\) is at least \(2^{-19}q^2\), and the treatment Bernstein exponent is at least \(2^{-22}q^2\), which proves (21).  The elementary one-variable optimizations
\[
 \sup_{q\ge1}qe^{-c_3q^3}\le(3ec_3)^{-1/3},
 \qquad
 \sup_{q\ge1}qe^{-c_2q^2}\le(2ec_2)^{-1/2}
\]
turn (21) into
\[
 P(\mathcal F_n)
 \le C_F\frac{b}{\kappa_n}. \tag{22}
\]
Since \(m\ge n/8\), \(b\le2\rho_n\) at \(s=1\).  Taking expectations in (20), using the maximal interval length two on the fallback, and applying (14) and (22), gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P|I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}|
 \le\frac{8C_rb}{\kappa_n}+\frac{2C_Fb}{\kappa_n}
 \le C_2\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}. \tag{23}
\]
Equations (8) and (13) imply \(\rho_n/\kappa_n<1\) in the asserted region, so (23) equals the claimed minimum order.

Finally, every unknown-cutoff rule induces a known-cutoff rule that ignores the supplied cutoff.  Therefore \(L_n^{\mathrm{known}}(\kappa_n)\le L_n(\kappa_n)\).  Combining this decision-theoretic inclusion, thm:known-cutoff-benchmark, and (23) yields
\[
 c_0\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n\}
 \le L_n^{\mathrm{known}}(\kappa_n)
 \le L_n(\kappa_n)
 \le C_2\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n\}.
\]
This proves the theorem.
added_lemmas.justification: This theorem supplies a completely evaluable honest procedure and the oracle expected-length guarantee on the Lipschitz face, with all grids, thresholds, fallbacks, and constants displayed.
added_lemmas.gap: Known-cutoff weak-first-stage inference and fixed-jump unknown-cutoff substitution do not imply uniform honest connected-length attainment when the first-stage jump vanishes; this theorem closes that gap for \(s=1\).
added_lemmas.consumer: For Lipschitz reduced forms, researchers can implement the four-fold rule and recover known-cutoff length whenever \(n\kappa_n^3\) exceeds the logarithmic location-search cost.

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose \(1<s\le2\), \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), and define \(\widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}}\) by def:profile-cutoff-center.  There are numerical constants \(a_{\mathrm p}=2^{-30}\), \(A_{\mathrm p}=64\), and a finite \(C_{\mathrm p}=C_{\mathrm p}(s,M)\) such that, if \(mH\kappa_n^2\ge C_{\mathrm p}\log(e/\kappa_n)\), there is an event \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}\), determined by folds one and two, for which
\[
 P(\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}^c)
 \le \frac{64}{H}\exp\{-a_{\mathrm p}mH\kappa_n^2\},
\]
the refinement bracket lies in \([c_P-4H,c_P+4H]\) on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}\), and, for every \(u\ge16/n\),
\[
 P\bigl(\{|\widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}}-c_P|>u\}\cap\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}\bigr)
 \le A_{\mathrm p}\exp\{-a_{\mathrm p}m\kappa_n^2u\}.
\]
No equality or compatibility between the left and right derivatives at \(c_P\) is assumed.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(\beta=s-1\in(0,1]\) and \(f_\ell=\mu_{D,P}^{\ell}\).  By ass:observable-holder-extensions, each side admits a differentiable extension satisfying
\[
 \lVert f_\ell'\rVert_\infty\le M,
 \qquad |f_\ell'(x)-f_\ell'(z)|\le M|x-z|^\beta. \tag{24}
\]
Consequently Taylor's identity and integration of (24) give, for points on the same side,
\[
 |f_\ell(x)-f_\ell(z)-f_\ell'(z)(x-z)|
 \le\frac{M}{s}|x-z|^s. \tag{25}
\]

We first verify the profile geometry.  In \(L^2[-1,1]\), the Gram determinant of \(1,u,(u-q)_+\) is
\[
 \det G_q=\frac{(1-q^2)^3}{18}>0,
 \qquad |q|\le\frac12, \tag{26}
\]
so the projection in def:profile-cutoff-center is well defined.  Direct integration gives
\[
 \lVert k_q\rVert_2^2
 =\langle S_q-\Pi_{\mathcal B_q}S_q,S_q\rangle
 =\frac{1-q^2}{8}\ge\frac{3}{32}. \tag{27}
\]
The projection coefficients are
\[
 \frac{(q-2)(q-1)}{4(q+1)},\qquad
 -\frac{3(q-1)}{4(q+1)},\qquad
 -\frac{3q}{(q-1)(q+1)}, \tag{28}
\]
respectively, whence \(\lVert k_q\rVert_\infty\le9\) uniformly on \(|q|\le1/2\).

Take a window \([z-r,z+r]\) containing \(c_P=z+qr\) with \(|q|\le1/2\).  Expanding the two side regressions at \(c_P\), equations (25)--(27) and the orthogonality of \(k_q\) to \(1,u,(u-q)_+\) yield
\[
 \begin{split}
 \frac1r\int_{z-r}^{z+r}f(x)k_q\!\left(\frac{x-z}{r}\right)dx
 &=d_P\lVert k_q\rVert_2^2+R(z,r,q),\\
 |R(z,r,q)|&\le18M(3r/2)^s.
 \end{split} \tag{29}
\]
The separate slopes disappear because their difference multiplies \((u-q)_+\), which is in \(\mathcal B_q\); this is the precise reason no derivative matching is needed.  If the whole window lies on one true side, the same calculation with a single Taylor polynomial gives
\[
 \left|\frac1r\int_{z-r}^{z+r}f(x)k_q\!\left(\frac{x-z}{r}\right)dx\right|
 \le18M(3r/2)^s. \tag{30}
\]
Since \(r\le H\), \(M H^s=\kappa_n/2^{12}\), \(s\le2\), and (27) holds, the remainder in (29)--(30) is smaller than \(\kappa_n/64\).  Together with \(d_P\ge\kappa_n\), this separates a jump-containing central window from a smooth window by more than \(3\kappa_n/4\) after division by \(\lVert k_q\rVert_2^2\).  Choose a coarse center for which \(c_P\) is in the central half of the window, and choose \(q\) within \(\kappa_n/2^{16}\) of \((c_P-z)/H\).  Formula (28), split at the two step locations, gives \(|J(z,H,q)-J(z,H,q')|\le256|q-q'|\).  The grid replacement therefore changes the normalized population profile by at most \(\kappa_n/256\).  Hence a fold-one window containing \(c_P\) is retained, while any retained window must meet \([c_P-H,c_P+H]\), on the event that every fold-one profile deviation is at most \(\kappa_n/16\).

For one profile summand, (27)--(28) and uniformity of \(X\) give absolute bound \(96/H\) and second moment at most \(96/H\).  The moment-generating-function inequality used in the proof of lem:rectangular-jump-scan-localization therefore gives
\[
 P\{|\widehat J_1-E_P\widehat J_1|>\kappa_n/16\}
 \le2\exp\{-2^{-28}mH\kappa_n^2\}. \tag{31}
\]
There are at most \(32/H\) coarse centers and \(1+2^{16}/\kappa_n\) profile locations per center.  The hypothesis \(mH\kappa_n^2\ge C_{\mathrm p}\log(e/\kappa_n)\) absorbs this factor and one half of the exponent, so the union bound in (31) is at most
\[
 \frac{32}{H}e^{-2^{-29}mH\kappa_n^2}. \tag{32}
\]
The preceding deterministic separation then places the retained hull inside \([c_P-4H,c_P+4H]\).

Condition on fold one and this coarse event.  Both flank intervals in def:profile-cutoff-center lie wholly on their declared true sides and have Lebesgue length \(H\).  Uniformity of \(X\) makes the population Gram matrix of the rescaled regressors \(1,(X-x_0)/H\) have smallest eigenvalue at least \(H/12\).  Applying (31) to its four entries shows that the empirical smallest eigenvalue is at least \(H/48\), except with probability at most \(8e^{-2^{-28}mH}\).  Equation (25), the normal equations, and the inverse bound \(48/H\) then give
\[
 \max_{x\in B}|\widehat p_\ell(x)-f_\ell(x)|\le\frac{\kappa_n}{64},
 \qquad \ell\in\{-,+\}, \tag{33}
\]
except with probability at most \(16e^{-2^{-28}mH\kappa_n^2}\).  Here the deterministic extrapolation error is at most \(72MH^s<\kappa_n/64\), and the stochastic coefficient error is at most \(\kappa_n/128\) under the stated lower bound on \(mH\kappa_n^2\), after enlarging \(C_{\mathrm p}\).  Clipping cannot increase the error because \(0\le f_\ell\le1\).  Let \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}\) be the intersection of the coarse event and (33).  Equations (32)--(33), with \(a_{\mathrm p}=2^{-30}\), prove the first probability display of the lemma.

It remains to analyze fold three.  Conditional on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}\), the two predictors are fixed and fold three is independent by ass:iid-sampling.  Put
\[
 q(x)=f_+(x)-f_-(x),\qquad \delta=\kappa_n/64.
\]
For \(0<w\le4H\), equations (24)--(25) give on the right of \(c_P\)
\[
 q(c_P+x)=d_P+ax+r(x),\qquad |a|\le2M,\qquad |r(x)|\le2Mx^s/s. \tag{34}
\]
For every real \(a\), direct minimization gives
\[
 \int_0^w(d_P+ax)^2dx
 =d_P^2w+d_Paw^2+\frac{a^2w^3}{3}
 \ge\frac{d_P^2w}{4}. \tag{35}
\]
Minkowski's inequality, (34), \(w\le4H\), and \(MH^s=\kappa_n/2^{12}\) therefore imply
\[
 \int_0^w q(c_P+x)^2\,dx\ge\frac{1}{8}\kappa_n^2w. \tag{36}
\]
If \(t>c_P\), the conditional population increase in the fold-three criterion is
\[
 \begin{split}
 E_P\{\widehat Q_3(t)-\widehat Q_3(c_P)\mid F_1,F_2\}
 &=\int_{c_P}^{t}\left[(f_+(x)-\widehat p_-(x))^2
 -(f_+(x)-\widehat p_+(x))^2\right]dx\\
 &\ge Q_t-2\delta\sqrt{(t-c_P)Q_t}-\delta^2(t-c_P),
 \end{split} \tag{37}
\]
where \(Q_t=\int_{c_P}^{t}q(x)^2dx\).  Equations (36)--(37) give
\[
 E_P\{\widehat Q_3(t)-\widehat Q_3(c_P)\mid F_1,F_2\}
 \ge2^{-5}\kappa_n^2(t-c_P). \tag{38}
\]
The calculation on the left is identical.  Notice that the conditional variance of one loss difference is bounded by
\[
 16\{q(X)^2+\delta^2\}\mathbf 1\{X\text{ lies between }c_P\text{ and }t\}, \tag{39}
\]
and its absolute value is at most \(4(|q(X)|+2\delta)\).  Thus the variance is controlled by the same integrated quadratic quantity that supplies the drift; no treatment-variance lower bound is being used.

Order the fold-three observations by \(X\).  For \(t>c_P+u\), the difference \(m\{\widehat Q_3(t)-\widehat Q_3(c_P)\}\) is a partial sum of the loss differences in (37).  On the dyadic block \(2^ju\le t-c_P<2^{j+1}u\), apply the elementary exponential supermartingale bound following from (39), with parameter truncated at the reciprocal of the displayed absolute bound.  Equations (36), (38), and (39) give
\[
 P\left\{\inf_{2^ju\le t-c_P<2^{j+1}u}
 \widehat Q_3(t)\le\widehat Q_3(c_P)\mid\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}\right\}
 \le8e^{-2^{-28}m\kappa_n^2 2^ju}. \tag{40}
\]
The same argument in decreasing \(X\)-order gives (40) to the left.  Replacing \(c_P\) by the closest grid point changes at most a strip of length \(1/n\); the restriction \(u\ge16/n\) absorbs this strip into the drift in (38).  Summing the two geometric series in (40), and using the bracket containment for \(u>4H\), gives
\[
 P\bigl(\{|\widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}}-c_P|>u\}\cap\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}\bigr)
 \le64e^{-2^{-30}m\kappa_n^2u}.
\]
This is the claimed localization tail.  Equations (26)--(29) show explicitly that the argument profiles out, rather than equates, the two side slopes.

added_lemmas.statement:
For \(1<s\le2\), under the unchanged class \(\mathcal P_n\) and the detectable-region condition \(T_n\gtrsim\log(e/\kappa_n)\), determine whether there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(s,M,v,\alpha\), such that
\[
 c\min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}+\frac1{n\kappa_n^3}\right\}
 \le L_n(\kappa_n)\le
 C\min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}+\frac1{n\kappa_n^3}\right\}.
\]
The upper side must use the degree-one profile localization in def:profile-cutoff-center and complete the fold-four bias-aware inversion.  The converse must construct matching slope-kink pairs in \(\mathcal P_n\).  In particular, prove or refute that the known-cutoff order \(\rho_n/\kappa_n\) is attained precisely on the face where \(n\kappa_n^2\rho_n\) is bounded below by a positive constant.  No cross-side derivative-matching condition may be added.

proposed.name: I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}
proposed.construction:
Let \(m=\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), discard observations with index larger than \(4m\), and put \(F_j=\{(j-1)m+1,\ldots,jm\}\), \(j=1,\ldots,4\).  Set
\[
 K_0(u)=\mathbf 1\{0\le u\le1\},\qquad
 H=\frac{\kappa_n}{2^{12}M},\qquad b=m^{-1/3},
\]
and, for \(V\in\{D,Y\}\), define the fixed-denominator contrast
\[
 \widehat\Delta_{j,h}^{V}(t)
 =\frac1{mh}\sum_{i\in F_j}V_i
 \left\{K_0\!\left(\frac{X_i-t}{h}\right)
 -K_0\!\left(\frac{t-X_i}{h}\right)\mathbf 1\{X_i<t\}\right\}.
\]
Let
\[
 \mathcal G_H=\left\{\frac14+\frac{kH}{64}:0\le k\le
 \left\lfloor\frac{32}{H}\right\rfloor\right\},
 \qquad N_H=|\mathcal G_H|,
\]
and retain
\[
 \mathcal A_H=\left\{t\in\mathcal G_H:
 \widehat\Delta_{1,H}^{D}(t)
 \ge\max_{q\in\mathcal G_H}\widehat\Delta_{1,H}^{D}(q)-\frac{\kappa_n}{8}\right\}.
\]
Write
\[
 B_H=\bigcup_{t\in\mathcal A_H}[t-H,t+H]\cap[1/4,3/4]
\]
and let \(\mathcal G_n(B_H)=(n^{-1}\mathbb Z)\cap B_H\), augmented, if necessary, by the two endpoints of every nonempty component of \(B_H\).  On this finite set define
\[
 \widehat c=\min\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{t\in\mathcal G_n(B_H)}
 \frac{\widehat\Delta_{2,H}^{D}(t)+\widehat\Delta_{3,H}^{D}(t)}2.
\]
If the displayed set is empty, set \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}=\Theta\).  Otherwise put
\[
 \widehat y(\widehat c)=\widehat\Delta_{4,b}^{Y}(\widehat c),
 \qquad \widehat d(\widehat c)=\widehat\Delta_{4,b}^{D}(\widehat c),
\]
\[
 L_\alpha=\log(32/\alpha),\qquad
 R_c=\frac{2^{16}L_\alpha}{m\kappa_n^2}+\frac1n,
\]
and
\[
 r_n=8Mb+16\kappa_n\frac{R_c}{b}+16MR_c
       +8\sqrt{\frac{L_\alpha}{mb}}.
\]
If \(R_c>H/8\), \(r_n>\kappa_n/8\), or \(\widehat d(\widehat c)<\kappa_n/2\), set \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}=\Theta\).  Otherwise let
\[
 A_n=\left\{\vartheta\in\Theta:
 |\widehat y(\widehat c)-\vartheta\widehat d(\widehat c)|\le2r_n\right\}.
\]
Set \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}=\operatorname{hull}(A_n)\) when \(A_n\ne\varnothing\), and otherwise set it equal to the singleton containing the projection of \(\widehat y(\widehat c)/\widehat d(\widehat c)\) onto \(\Theta\).  Smallest-argument tie breaking and the stated finite grids make this a measurable map of the sample.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The Lipschitz theorem needs the directive's complete deterministic four-fold map, including grids, tie breaking, bias radius, denominator certification, and fallbacks.

proposed.name: \widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}}
proposed.construction:
Suppose \(1<s\le2\), put \(m=\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), and use the four deterministic folds \(F_j=\{(j-1)m+1,\ldots,jm\}\).  Set
\[
 H=\left(\frac{\kappa_n}{2^{12}M}\right)^{1/s}.
\]
For \(q\in[-1/2,1/2]\), let \(S_q(u)=\mathbf 1\{u\ge q\}\), let \(\mathcal B_q=\operatorname{span}\{1,u,(u-q)_+\}\) in \(L^2[-1,1]\), and define
\[
 k_q=S_q-\Pi_{\mathcal B_q}S_q.
\]
For a fold \(j\), a center \(z\), a radius \(r\), and \(a=z+qr\), define
\[
 \widehat J_{j}(z,r,q)=
 \frac{1}{mr\lVert k_q\rVert_2^2}
 \sum_{i\in F_j}D_i k_q\!\left(\frac{X_i-z}{r}\right)
 \mathbf 1\{|X_i-z|\le r\}.
\]
On fold one, take centers on the \(H/8\)-mesh in \([1/4-H,3/4+H]\) and \(q\) on the \(\kappa_n/2^{16}\)-mesh in \([-1/2,1/2]\).  Retain every window \([z-H,z+H]\) for which \(\widehat J_1(z,H,q)\ge\kappa_n/2\) for at least one such \(q\), and let \(B=[A,B_+]\) be the connected hull of the retained windows, intersected with \([1/4-2H,3/4+2H]\).  If there is no retained window, return \(\widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}}=1/2\).

Conditionally on fold one, fit by ordinary least squares on fold two a degree-one polynomial \(\widehat p_-\) over \([A-2H,A-H]\) and a degree-one polynomial \(\widehat p_+\) over \([B_++H,B_++2H]\), using on each flank the rescaled regressors \(1,(X-x_0)/H\), where \(x_0\) is that flank's left endpoint, and clip both fitted values to \([0,1]\).  The empirical Gram matrix is \(m^{-1}\sum_{i\in F_2}\mathbf 1\{X_i\text{ is in the flank}\}(1,(X_i-x_0)/H)^{\mathsf T}(1,(X_i-x_0)/H)\).  If either such \(2\times2\) matrix has smallest eigenvalue below \(H/48\), return \(\widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}}=1/2\).  Otherwise, on the finite grid
\[
 \mathcal T_n=(n^{-1}\mathbb Z)\cap B
\]
augmented by the endpoints of \(B\), define
\[
 \widehat Q_3(t)=\frac1m\sum_{i\in F_3}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B\}
 \left[(D_i-\widehat p_-(X_i))^2\mathbf 1\{X_i<t\}
 +(D_i-\widehat p_+(X_i))^2\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge t\}\right]
\]
and set
\[
 \widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}}=\min\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{t\in\mathcal T_n}\widehat Q_3(t).
\]
Thus the coarse statistic is the coefficient of a discontinuity after profiling out a continuous degree-one fit and a slope kink, while the refinement separately fits the two degree-one side regressions and classifies each observation by its residual loss.

proposed_core_edits.reason: For \(s>1\), separate degree-one flank fits and residual-loss classification profile out the derivative kink under the original observable class.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A uniform higher-smoothness fold-four length upper bound with the \(MR_c/\kappa_n\) term and a matching same-class slope-kink lower pair.
open_obligations.obstruction: The profile center now localizes at \(R_c\asymp(n\kappa_n^2)^{-1}\), but separate one-sided H\"older extensions allow the transformed-outcome derivative to kink at the cutoff. Moving the center by \(R_c\) therefore creates order \(MR_c/\kappa_n\), and no frozen lower construction yet certifies that this term is necessary.
open_obligations.attempted: The raw intercept-jump scan was replaced by a degree-one profile score. Orthogonal projection of the step indicator against \(1,u,(u-q)_+\) proves population separation and a sequential Bernstein argument proves the desired localization tail. Propagating this tail through fixed-center inversion exposes, rather than removes, the additional \(1/(n\kappa_n^3)\) term.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The profile identity already closes the localization component without derivative matching: for \(|q|\le1/2\), the residualized step satisfies \(\lVert k_q\rVert_2^2=(1-q^2)/8\ge3/32\), and the slope-kink regressor \((u-q)_+\) is projected out.  The resulting center has conditional tail
\[
 P\{|\hat c_{\mathrm{prof}}-c_P|>u,\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}\}
 \le64\exp\{-2^{-30}m\kappa_n^2u\}.
\]
Thus its natural error is \(R_c\asymp(n\kappa_n^2)^{-1}\).  For the transformed-outcome jump, the unchanged class permits a derivative kink, so moving the center by \(R_c\) contributes order \(MR_c/\kappa_n\asymp(n\kappa_n^3)^{-1}\) to LATE length, in addition to the known-cutoff term \(\rho_n/\kappa_n\).  The equality
\[
 \frac1{n\kappa_n^3}\lesssim\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad n\kappa_n^2\rho_n\gtrsim1
\]
explains the proposed oracle face.  What remains open is a uniform fold-four upper proof with this radius and an in-class slope-kink lower pair attaining the same second term.

prose_updates.tldr: The paper studies fixed-\(\alpha\) expected length of connected honest intervals for fuzzy-RD LATE when the compliance jump and its unknown cutoff weaken jointly. The location-mixture construction proves a finite-sample nonshrinking converse below the signal-to-entropy boundary. At \(s=1\), an explicit four-fold scan--refine--invert map attains the known-cutoff order once \(n\kappa_n^3\) dominates \(\log(e/\kappa_n)\). For \(s>1\), a new degree-one profile criterion localizes the cutoff without derivative matching, but the same-class interval frontier remains the explicit bracket question \(L_n\asymp\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n+1/(n\kappa_n^3)\}\).

project_justification.gap: Known-cutoff weak fuzzy-RD inference and fixed-jump unknown-cutoff localization do not characterize honest connected LATE-interval length when both the compliance denominator and its location weaken. In particular, neither result controls the transformed-outcome effect of an unrestricted cross-cutoff slope kink.
project_justification.niche: The joint experiment combines a nonconvex location union, a causal outcome--treatment ratio, and fixed-level connected-length loss. The Lipschitz face has an attainable oracle reduction, while for \(s>1\) cutoff localization and post-localization slope-kink bias are distinct statistical components.
project_justification.fill: The project gives one observable reduced-form class, embeds outcome-invariant monotone location mixtures to prove the finite-sample converse, supplies a fully explicit oracle-order four-fold interval at \(s=1\), and proves a slope-profiled \(s>1\) cutoff estimator with exponential localization. The remaining higher-smoothness contribution is honestly posed as the bracket with terms \(\rho_n/\kappa_n\) and \(1/(n\kappa_n^3)\), including a matching slope-kink converse.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: One-sided observable treatment and outcome regressions admit radius-\(M\), order-\(s\) H\"older extensions, with no equality imposed on their derivatives at the cutoff. The proved \(s=1\) interval uses deterministic four-fold rectangular scanning and fixed-center inversion. For \(s>1\), the proved cutoff component residualizes a candidate jump against a continuous broken line, fits separate degree-one flank regressions, and refines by cross-fold residual-loss classification.

prose_updates.related_work: Noack and Rothe (2024) supply the known-cutoff bias-aware Anderson--Rubin benchmark, but not unknown-cutoff connected expected length. Porter and Yu (2015) prove fixed-jump cutoff localization in a sharp-design model; the theorem here instead permits \(\kappa_n\to0\) and proves oracle-order honest length at \(s=1\). Frick, Munk, and Sieling (2014) and Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014) inform scan and maximal-control architecture, but neither gives this causal localization-to-length result. M{\"u}ller and Song (1997) and Tuvaandorj (2020) study location experiments rather than weak-denominator LATE intervals. Armstrong and Koles{\'a}r (2018) treat convex fixed-index classes. Madrid Padilla, Yu, Wang, and Rinaldo (2022) study aligned multivariate change channels without the monotone fuzzy-RD causal constraints. Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas (2025 version) use Bayesian unknown-cutoff inference, and Arai, Otsu, and Seo (2026) treat fuzzy and unknown-discontinuity extensions separately. The proved results here are the finite-sample location-mixture converse, the \(s=1\) oracle-attainment theorem, and slope-robust profile localization for \(s>1\); the full higher-smoothness interval bracket is not claimed as determined or sharp.
prose_updates.interpretation: At \(s=1\), the information \(n\kappa_n^3\) pays the logarithmic search cost and the independent fourth-fold inversion then has the same \(n^{-1/3}/\kappa_n\) length as if the cutoff were known. For \(s>1\), profiling a candidate step against \(1,u,(u-q)_+\) removes the side-slope mismatch from cutoff localization and yields error \(R_c\asymp(n\kappa_n^2)^{-1}\). The unchanged class nevertheless lets a transformed-outcome derivative kink turn that location error into LATE error of order \(MR_c/\kappa_n\asymp1/(n\kappa_n^3)\).
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Oracle-order strong-signal interval length is proved only at \(s=1\). For \(1<s\le2\), the cutoff itself is now localized by a proved slope-profiled criterion with tail \(\exp(-c n\kappa_n^2u)\), but the complete fourth-fold honesty and expected-length calculation with the \(MR_c\) term, and the matching in-class slope-kink lower pairs, remain open. The exact fixed-\(\alpha\) critical-window law also remains open.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The Wald interpretation, the known-cutoff benchmark, and the finite-sample outcome-invariant location-mixture converse retain their full stated scope. The explicit oracle-attainment result is uniform only on the Lipschitz face \(s=1\). For \(s>1\), only slope-robust cutoff localization is proved; the bracket \(\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n+1/(n\kappa_n^3)\}\) and its oracle subface \(n\kappa_n^2\rho_n\gtrsim1\) are questions, not conclusions. No cross-side derivative compatibility, latent-cell smoothness, adaptation, disconnected-set, or Bayesian-calibration claim is added.
